extracted.intended_audience: European patent applicants, their representatives (patent attorneys) and EPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes substantive and procedural examination standards and requirements from the European Patent Office Guidelines (01 March 2021), covering filing dates, consultations, oral proceedings (incl. videoconference), time limits, claim/description consistency, patentability guidance for computer-implemented inventions, biotechnology (stem cells, antibodies, plants), and second medical use claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'earlier application' for divisional filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'earlier application' in Article 76(1) EPC and Rule 36 EPC is to be understood as a patent application filed at least one day before the divisional application; thus, a divisional application cannot be filed on the same day as its parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies timing for divisional filing priority: same-day filing of parent and divisional is not acceptable. See Section A‑IV.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euro‑PCT corrected international filing date (Rule 20.5bis PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Euro‑PCT applications where an element was subsequently corrected under Rule 20.5bis PCT during the international phase and the international filing date was not postponed, the EPO will consider as filing date only the date on which the complete correct documents were filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this affects priority claims and prior art, the applicant will be given the opportunity (within 2 months after request) to file a written statement to choose either (a) continue with the original international filing date and base examination on the originally filed (partially erroneous) documents, or (b) accept the date when correct documents were filed as the filing date and recognize those as the original application documents. The applicant may also proactively make this request within the 31‑month period to avoid delays. See Section C‑III.1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified 'consultation' category and effects on deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone and personal consultations with the examination department/first examiner have been combined into a single category 'consultation'; videoconference is preferred but telephone is allowed on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consultation should preferably be held as a videoconference (allows document presentation, participation of others, identity verification). Oral statements during a consultation that substantively address objections raised in an earlier communication may result in the examiner cancelling any running time limit. Documents admissibly submitted by email during the consultation may be sufficient to preserve an ongoing deadline. See Section C‑VII.2 and C‑VII.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of requesting decision according to the state of the file
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for oral proceedings is pending when the applicant files a request for a decision according to the state of the file, the Examining Division will interpret the latter as an implicit withdrawal of the pending request for oral proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a decision according to the state of the file, freshly presented arguments of the applicant in response to a communication must be considered by issuing either a regular reasoned decision or a further communication. Minutes of a consultation do not meet the standards of a communication under Article 94(3) and thus cannot be the basis of a decision according to the state of the file. See Sections C‑IV.15.1 and C‑IV.15.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings before Examining Divisions by videoconference
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings before the Examining Division are to be held by videoconference; in‑person proceedings at EPO premises only if there are serious reasons against videoconference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious reasons are limited and include individual participant issues (e.g., proven visual impairment preventing following on screen) or subject‑matter needs (e.g., demonstration/inspection requiring haptic features). General objections to videoconferencing reliability or lack of equipment will not, as a rule, qualify. Requests for in‑person proceedings should be filed early (preferably with the request for oral proceedings); granting is at the division's discretion. A rejection must be briefly substantiated and is not appealable. See Section E‑III.1 and E‑III.2.2 and President's Decision dated 17 Dec 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings before Opposition Divisions by videoconference (pilot project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings in opposition proceedings may be held as a videoconference if the parties agree; under the pilot project they will be held by videoconference during the pilot period unless serious reasons against it exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot project extension: oral proceedings before opposition divisions were to be held by videoconference from 4 January 2021 until at least 15 September 2021. Only very exceptional serious reasons (as above) will justify postponement to in‑person hearings. See Section D‑IV.3.2 and President's Decision dated 10 Nov 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of written submissions during oral proceedings held as videoconference
rubrics_metrics.description: If oral proceedings are held as a videoconference, documents filed subsequently as referred to in Rule 50 EPC must be filed by email; signatures may be a string of characters or a facsimile signature indicating the person's name and position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended application documents must be attached as PDF and comply with the WIPO Standard for Filing and Processing in Electronic Form (Annex F). If an attachment is not PDF, doesn't comply, or is illegible/incomplete, the party must be informed during the videoconference; if deficiencies cannot be remedied during the videoconference or within the time limit set, that document (or the illegible/incomplete part) is deemed not to have been received. No paper documents are required to confirm documents filed by email. All submissions made by email during a videoconference must be annexed to the minutes unless exceptions under Rule 144 EPC apply. See Section E‑III.8.5.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical preparation and contingency for videoconference oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will receive an email confirming date, time and videoconference contact details (link or other suitable means) and any further information; if the videoconference does not start at the agreed time the division will contact the representative by telephone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the connection cannot be established for technical reasons, the videoconference shall be terminated and a new summons to oral proceedings shall be issued. See Section E‑III.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Rule 134 EPC for outages of electronic filing/communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension of time limits under Rule 134(1) EPC applies in cases where one of the means of electronic filing provided by the EPO is not available, regardless of document restrictions on that filing means; Rule 134(2) EPC may apply to a general breakdown of any means of electronic communication accepted by the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section E‑III.1.6.2 takes into account the Notice of 22 Oct 2020 concerning procedures/safeguards for outages. The guidelines explicitly list the time limits that fall within the scope of Rule 134 EPC and mention cases where extension under Rule 134 EPC is not available. Means currently include Web‑Form Filing, Online Filing (OLF), New Online Filing (CMS), ePCT and fax. See Section E‑VIII.1 and E‑III.1.6.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of the description to amended claims (Article 84 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where part of the subject‑matter of the description and/or drawings is not covered by the claims, the description must be adapted to the claims to avoid inconsistencies between claims and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embodiments in the description no longer covered by the independent claims must be deleted (e.g., alternatives no longer covered) unless they can reasonably be considered useful for highlighting specific aspects of the amended claims; if retained, it must be prominently stated that the embodiment is not covered by the claims (T 1808/06). Claim‑like clauses must be deleted or amended prior to grant, particularly if inconsistent with claimed subject‑matter or merely repeat the claimed subject‑matter in a very literal manner (considered 'an irrelevant and unnecessary reduplication' not fulfilling Rule 48(1)(c)). See Sections F‑IV.4.3 and F‑IV.4.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical contribution of data structures, data formats and DBMS for computer‑implemented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance explains under which circumstances a data structure or data format may contribute to the technical character of the invention; database management systems and information retrieval processes may be considered technical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section G‑II.3.6.3 clarifies when data structures/formats can contribute to technical character. Section G‑II.3.6.4 states that database management systems are technical systems installed on computers to perform the technical tasks of storing and retrieving data using various data structures for efficient data management; thus such processes are not excluded from patentability under Article 52(2) EPC. See G‑II.3.6 and G‑II.3.6.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of certain human stem cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluripotent human stem cells including human embryonic stem cells, their use, or products derived therefrom do not fall under the patenting prohibition of Article 53(a) and Rule 28(1)(c) if the application has a filing or priority date on or after 5 June 2003 and if the technical teaching of the invention allows the use of parthenogenetically activated human oocytes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects established case law; see Sections G‑II.5.2 and G‑II.5.3 for scope and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of plant/animal material producible exclusively by essentially biological processes (G 3/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material allowing regeneration of whole plants, such as cells, seeds, cuttings, etc., are subject to the exclusion of patentability under Article 53(b) EPC if the plants from which this material is derived can be exclusively obtained by means of an essentially biological process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion does not apply to patent applications and patents with a filing or priority date prior to 1 July 2017. See Sections G‑II.5.3 and G‑II.5.4 and G 3/19 (OJ EPO 2020, A119).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria for antibody claims
rubrics_metrics.description: New antibody‑focused examination practice addresses admissible structural/functional antibody definitions in claims and the basis for examining inventive step in this field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: a structural antibody definition must reference at least all six CDR regions; broader structural definitions must be supported by experimental evidence. If an antibody is defined by target antigen/epitope, the antigen/epitope must be referenced without open‑ended formulations (e.g., broad sequence identity ranges or 'comprising'); negative features (antigens/epitopes not bound) are possible. If solely functional features are used and prior art discloses an antibody binding the identical antigen, the burden of proof of novelty lies with the applicant. Product‑by‑process definitions are possible if the general requirements are met, but claims relying on immunization methods with non‑100% identical sequences of the alleged antigen may fail Article 84 EPC. See Section G‑II.5.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second medical indication — requirement of direct therapeutic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: For a second medical indication, the requirement is whether a substance or a mixture of substances has a direct therapeutic effect as an active ingredient for a specific medical use due to its chemical properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the effect is merely a physical property (e.g., a shielding effect or use of a substance as a filler to protect sensitive tissue), such use is to be regarded as a device and not patentable under Article 54(5) EPC (T 1758/15). See Section G‑VI.7.1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of waiver of right to receive further communication under Rule 71(3) EPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility of waiving the right to receive a further communication under Rule 71(3) EPC has been abolished and chapters referring to the now unavailable waiver have been deleted from the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural change in Part C affecting how applicants may or may not relinquish their right to further communications; see the Notice dated 26 May 2020 and related updates in Part C.
